title: Chapter 133: Nightmare Difficulty
html:
Pei Hu staggered backward, face drained of color, and barely caught his balance.

“Are you alright? What happened?” Wang Wenlong and Xia Meili behind them rushed over immediately.

“Ignore him. It’s nothing.” Wang Hailong’s legs trembled and one cheek twitched, but he forced himself to sound calm. “Just a room full of mannequins.”

Despite bracing themselves, the other three recoiled when they looked inside. More than twenty mannequins were frightening enough. Every one staring in the same direction—some with their necks twisted a full 180 degrees—was impossible to prepare for.

“I wondered why the earlier classrooms were so tame. They were building up to this ‘surprise.’” The calmest among them, Wang Wenlong switched on his phone’s flashlight.

“Wenlong, the boss said to not use the phone inside the scenario,” Xia Meili warned.

“What he doesn’t know won’t hurt him.” Wang Wenlong swept the beam across the mannequins’ glossy bodies. “They’re all props. None blinked when the light crossed their eyes. Wait—I see two name tags!”

“Where?”

“One is pinned to a uniform.” Wang Wenlong aimed the beam. A tag hung from the lapel of a mannequin in the middle, while another lay on the farthest desk. Reaching either required passing between rows of figures.

“This boss sure is immoral!”

“Thank goodness all five of us came. Anyone attempting this alone would lose their mind.”

“Enough praising him and undermining ourselves.” Wang Hailong paced until feeling returned to his legs. “We still have time, and this room probably holds more than two tags. We’re going in, and we’re searching every corner.”

“Brother Long, think this through. Four thousand yuan isn’t worth our lives!” Pei Hu had not recovered from the first shock and could barely think straight.

“It’s not that serious. Stop talking nonsense and get over here.” Wang Hailong dragged him to the sealed classroom.

“Why do I have to go first?” Pei Hu’s survival instincts flared.

“Because if I don’t watch you, you’ll abandon us.” Wang Hailong shoved him inside, then addressed Dou Menglu and Xia Meili. “We three men will go first. If anything happens, come get us.”

“Okay, be careful.”

“We’ll be fine. Wenlong already proved they’re mannequins.” Wang Hailong and Wenlong entered. From the lectern, the three surveyed the classroom and immediately broke out in goose bumps.

“Wonderful. The mannequins fill every aisle. There’s barely room to move.”

“Pei Hu, since you’re so frightened, take the tag in the middle. Wenlong, search the drawers. I’ll retrieve the one at the back.” Wang Hailong assumed a leader’s authority. Pei Hu disliked the assignment but had no choice.

Before stepping down, Pei Hu recoiled again. “Brother Long, their eyes are moving!”

“Would it kill you to stay quiet?” Pei Hu’s panic was making Wang Hailong nervous too.

“It’s the uncanny valley effect. Anything too humanlike naturally makes us uncomfortable,” Wang Wenlong explained, though even he sounded unconvinced.

“Both of you, quiet. The countdown has started, and we need every tag within twenty minutes. Stop wasting time.” Wang Hailong forced himself toward the farthest desk.

“Don’t be angry, Brother Long.” Pei Hu hesitantly approached the center desk. As he stepped down from the lectern, his belly bumped a standing mannequin and made it sway.

“Whoever designed this place must have suffered terrible trauma to imagine something this sick…” Before Pei Hu finished, something bumped his back. “Wenlong?”

He turned to look, and Wang Wenlong was several meters away from him.

“Who touched me?” His gaze settled on the still-trembling mannequin. It was lifelike enough to be mistaken for a real person at a glance. “Was it this mannequin?”

Pei Hu shuddered and hurried away before he could find out. At the center desk sat a girl in a different uniform, its fabric soaked in blood as though her final moments had been horrific.

He stared at the tag on her lapel, drew a deep breath, and reached for it. Just before his fingertip brushed the girl’s neck, her head shifted away from the window.

“F*ck me!” Pei Hu instantly pulled his hand back like he had been shocked by electricity.

“Did it move? Is this a real person?” Wang Hailong was still approaching the rear desk, and Wang Wenlong remained nearby. Their presence gave Pei Hu enough courage to reach again and seize the tag.

“I got it.” A ridiculous wave of triumph filled him—until he tried to pull away and discovered a cord tied from the tag to a noose around the girl’s neck.

“F*ck! Was this really necessary?” At that moment, he wanted to split the boss in two. Still gripping the tag, he circled the mannequin, switched on his phone for light, and bent close to untie the knot.

As the phone’s glow crossed the girl’s face, her expression changed. Pei Hu noticed nothing. Standing behind her, head bowed, he focused entirely on the knot.

Then Wang Wenlong inhaled sharply and whispered, “Something’s wrong. Why do I feel as though this mannequin has been following me?”

“You’re imagining things.” Encouraged by his progress, Pei Hu laughed. He turned back to the knot—and found the seated girl’s head facing him. His living face and her lifeless one were less than half a finger apart.
